about: Machine learning engineer and computational biologist at NVIDIA: building scientific LLMs, biological sequence models, and scalable research software. Former principal investigator at the National Renewable Energy Lab connecting computational modeling with experimental biology and chemistry.

On NVIDIA’s BioNeMo team, I develop Nemotron post-training and evaluation workflows for genomics and chemistry using supervised fine-tuning and GRPO. I also optimize distributed model training and build modular, Hugging Face-compatible research tools.

Previously, I led ML data-infrastructure projects for NVIDIA’s autonomous-vehicle team. At NREL, I led research across protein language modeling, metabolic modeling, and machine learning for molecular and materials discovery, including collaborations that used computational results to guide experiments.

My leadership experience includes leading 2–3 ML engineers, coordinating cross-team technical delivery, leading a $1.8M research program across three institutions, and mentoring graduate students and postdoctoral researchers.

current.title: Machine Learning Engineer
resumeBullets: Built a framework to extend LLMs to arbitrary new modalities, implementing support in NeMo RL, AutoModel, and Dynamo. Post-trained a DNA-conditioned Nemotron with SFT/GRPO against a newly created dataset and eval metric to reach frontier-level performance

Optimized and benchmarked PyTorch/Transformer Engine training across Hopper, Blackwell, and Rubin. Achieved 1.69× Mixtral throughput on 8xB300 GPUs, and nearly 70% MFU with Llama 3-70B context-parallel pretraining on GB300 NVL72.
Led BioNeMo’s shift to modular, Hugging Face-compatible training recipes, aligning customer and cross-team requirements; authored the initial integration and published the Recipes release.
Partnered with biotechnology, genomics, and diagnostics customers on protein-model training and evaluation, Transformer Engine/MoE requirements, and multimodal research scoping.
